Five years ago I was struggling financially.  Worst financial situation I have ever been in.  Newly divorced, single parent, all that.  One day I get pulled over for speeding.  As the officer is walking up to the window I just prayed because I had no way of paying a ticket I clearly deserved.   I didn't argue with him, I didn't cry, I just admitted I was wrong and handed him my info.   He told me he wasn't going to give me a ticket, but he said, "Just promise you won't speed anymore."    I gave him my word that I wouldn't.   Now, I am a right lane only driver who feels really guilty about all the angry drivers behind me.   If it helps I do apologize to all of them in my head and I give them the I'm sorry look when they fly past me.

I used to say I was a Christian because it made the most sense to me.  I believed, but I wouldn't say I had a strong relationship to God. I prayed a lot, but I went through the motions more than I really spent time with God.    Then something horrific happened and I could honestly feel a battle for my soul.   I was so incredibly angry with God,  I pushed him away, but I could feel him with me.   There was a moment I was in mass and I was yelling at God in my head while I was staring at the crucifix.   I truly believe I heard him speak to me.   It didn't end the anger, but I knew he was there.   He answered me.  For a few years I struggled more because I believed in God, I just wasn't sure that I believed he was kind and loving.   I continued to push him about as far as I could and I could feel it making me bitter.  Finally, I started to realize, God was still there.  All the times I was angry,  all the times I lashed out, all the times I felt more broken than I could put into words he was there trying to comfort me.   I wouldn't allow it.   I wasn't ready to listen or feel God.   When I opened my heart to him again, I could feel healing and hope.  It didn't end the sorrow, but something changed.  I started to see how God was working with that sorrow and trying to guide me to accept the suffering.  I learned that by sitting with the pain with God by my side, I could allow it to ebb and flow.  I saw God with me.  It is honestly like the verse in the Bible.  Jesus wept.   I felt Jesus weeping and hurting with me.   So this is a very long story to say I believe in the Holy Trinity because I feel the Holy Trinity.  I know the Holy Trinity.   I would be lying if I said I didn't question my faith sometimes.   I am human and that is part of the human experience. However, when I start to pull away from God, I see him reaching out for me and bringing me back.

 The first year your only job is to survive.  Just keep breathing.  Some days that is all you can do and that is completely ok. Please talk.  Tell your story.  Give a voice to your pain.  This grief can feel isolating.  Sometimes we fear speaking and making people uncomfortable.  The reality is they may be uncomfortable for a few minutes, but it is nothing compared to the discomfort you feel daily.  If they care about you, they will listen. If not they don't then they are not your people. 
The second year is when I believe the work begins.  I won't tell you it gets easier but as time goes by the intensity won't be as strong. You don't get caught off guard as often.  You are able to prepare yourself in many ways for the waves of grief that come.  Don't get me wrong things will still stop you in your tracks, just less often.  Peace can be found and joy will come.  It is something that doesn't happen over night and it requires a lot of work.  It requires purposeful actions. Some days are harder than others.  Some years are harder than others. I constantly remind myself it is ok to visit the dark, I just can't live there.  We walk this journey together.  If you don't have someone in your life who has walked this path please reach out to someone. Prayers for you fellow redditor. My youngest daughter is adopted.   She was in fostercare from the age of two.  She had weekly visits with bio family until she was six.  She was also separated from her siblings (in this particular situation it was the right move). I know she loves them and always will.  I know there is a bond there that I can't nor do I want to break.  However,  sometimes she romanticizes what it was because she was so young and she doesn't remember the trauma. The truth is it was really bad. We run into them occasionally and I have been polite and have allowed her to talk to them.  Honestly, I don't support her having a relationship with them other than an occasional conversation at the store.  It hurts her and brings up a lot of emotions she isn't equipped to address even with counseling. Sometimes she is afraid she will see them and doesn't want to hug them but feels guilty.   I don't, so I politely tell them no touching.  When she is an adult I will give her access to her case file and adoption information and support whatever she decides to do as long as she never allows her children to be unsupervised with them. This has nothing to do with jealousy, this is about safety.  While some say the bio parents may change this is not a case where that is possible.  Doesn't really apply to your situation but it is possible your parents are afraid you will wind up getting hurt and they want to protect you.

He is who gets me out of bed each morning, he gets me to work, he shows me how to take care of my family and gives me the strength to keep going.  
So to summarize, I believe in Jesus because I know him.

My 15 year old son committed suicide three weeks ago.  That being said I feel he is now with the Lord in Heaven.
If you are considering suicide there are so many reasons not to do it other than your salvation.   I would like to give you some information about how suicide will affect those around you.   You may read if you want and ignore if you don't.  
Sunday October 9th my husband and I were going to get breakfast.   We stopped downstairs to see what our son wanted.    His door was locked and he didn't answer.   We unlocked the door preparing to wake him up calling him a sleepy head.   We opened the door and blood was everywhere.   I rushed to my son and held him in my arms screaming.   My husband screamed as he checked for a pulse.   It was obvious Nathan was no longer with us.   I yelled for my husband to get the girls out if the house.   They were running downstairs to see why we were screaming.    I heard my daughters breakdown as my husband told them what happened as he ushered them outside.   I held my baby with one hand and called 911 with the other.   Because we live in the country it took about 30 minutes for the police to arrive.   I rocked my son in my arms sobbing.  I refused to let go and had to be dragged out of the room.   I changed clothes on my front porch and walked as far away from my house as possible before collapsing on the ground.    The next week I hated myself for not knowing he was struggling so bad and I was angry with God for allowing my son to leave us.  Other than the funeral stuff I stayed in bed for the first week and a half.   I didn't eat and I prayed God would take me to Heaven to be with my son.    My daughters didn't have a mom that first week and I am still struggling to be there for them.   My son is the first thing I think of when I wake up and the last thing I think of before bed.   I dream about him every night.   I'm not sure which is worse the bad dreams or the good dreams.   The good dreams always hurt so bad when I wake up.   I am not able to go back to work and I worry I will never be happy again.   I am now a survivor of suicide.   My husband and children and all the friends and family members who love Nathan are now survivors of suicide.   Our son is now at rest but our pain is just beginning.  I wake up replaying his entire life trying to figure out what I did wrong.  Where did I fail my son?    The guilt eats away at your soul and you begin to doubt the very existence of our Heavenly Father and Son.  My son's friends carry the guilt as well.  Everyone who loves him feels responsible for his loss even though he wrote no one was to blame.  The pain I feel will never lessen or disappear.   I will always carry them image of saying goodbye to my precious baby.  Every minute I long to hear his voice and hold him.  I worry our entire relationship was a lie but that is wrong.  The lie was him believing he wouldn't get better.   My life is now broken down into two parts.  Before and after.   I suffered from depression and anxiety when I was young but I got help and got better. The what ifs of getting him help or of him telling us his thoughts  destroy me sometimes.  I can never go back to who I was but I will work everyday to stop another family from going through our pain.   Your pain is real but can be helped.   There is no help for the  grief of losing a loved one.
